decisions.text: Client and investment records stay intact on dev and production; the dev server may be cleaned. There is no standalone cleanup project: client data is reformed only when a change needs it, nothing is lost, the step is rehearsed on dev against a masked copy, duplicate investments are reversed with both rows kept, and duplicate accounts are merged only for pairs the maintainer confirms. Answers question rows 1 and 9.
decisions.status: In force; Phase D runs only when a change needs it

decisions.text: When the admin records an investment, the client sees it as a receipt labelled with the category the admin chose: earlier investment, monthly investment or correction. Answers question row 2.

No automatic maturity. The admin enters a maturity date per client fund holding, a Maturities dashboard lists them, and the admin is prompted at every admin launch for maturities due within 30 days and overdue ones. Every recording counts and the admin manages them. Answers question row 3; the resolutions are set by DEC-15.
Nominee: the nominee's name and their relation to the account holder. Answers question row 4.

Public signups are not in use; clients are onboarded only by the admin, so the signup redirect to app.beonedge.in is dropped. The signup application review stays as it is, and the onboarding process is audited for bugs instead. Answers question row 5.
Client ratings and comments on the app are wanted and are visible to admins only, with the client profile; nothing is public. Answers question rows 6 and 10.
AutoPay is not activated until the maintainer says so, so AutoPay on the web is not pursued. App-update announcement emails keep going to every active client. Answers question row 7.

Value updates are entered monthly as the amount gained since investment. Each update is kept as a record and the client is notified every time. Dashboards show simple return % as the main figure and annualised XIRR as a secondary column. Answers question row 8.

Start a new SIP means an admin-tracked schedule: monthly amount, fund, start month and number of months. Each monthly recording links to a month and the client sees N of M months paid. There is no automatic collection. The maturity date is per client fund holding. Answers question row 11.

An audited admin contact correction for clients who have not set a password, which retires old links and sends the invite to the corrected address. Closed accounts can release their email and phone. Original contacts are kept in an append-only history. Answers question row 12.
Invite links stay short, at 10 minutes. The admin can send a new invite in one obvious action, including after the old one expired or was cancelled. Answers question row 13.
Setting a password does not verify the email; the email code step stays. Answers question row 14.
No reference number of any kind (UTR or other) is assigned to or kept on investments the admin records. Recordings keep category, amount, date and fund. Answers question row 16.

Payments: nothing is added or changed; the maintainer asked only for bug fixes and for payments to be disabled. AutoPay and everything related to the payment gateway are halted until the maintainer says to resume them. Answers question row 17.

Maturity: the admin is notified first, by the launch prompt from 30 days before the date. The options are (1) withdraw the invested amount with returns, (2) reinvest the previous amount as a one-time investment and then start recording the next SIP, (3) increase the SIP's time period. The options never pop up for the client by themselves: the admin either resolves directly after talking to the client, or sends the options to that client, who then gets an email and an in-app notification and can choose in the app. Both the client and the admin can decide. Answers question row 18.

The Record action on the admin user page offers a Monthly investment category. Every recording has a history with the date it was recorded, kept as a ledger the admin sees and reflected in the client's app.
The integration suite may run in a local container with a throwaway PostgreSQL.

Clients pay SIPs and investments directly to the company, and the admin records them. Whether the gateway is on or off must not affect how quickly and clearly a client sees their investment in the app.
The maintainer delegates working out what else this kind of app needs, and simplifying complex flows so both client and admin have a seamless experience.

Phase F go-ahead: build F1 (recorded date on the admin ledger), F2 (option 3 extends the SIP) and F3 (the admin sends maturity options to a client, who chooses in the app) with the conservative defaults of Q-030 to Q-032: the client's pick waits for the admin to confirm, the admin fills in the figures, and an extension moves the maturity date by the months added unless the admin changes it.

Plan plans/admin-improvements.md approved ("Yes I do", in answer to approving the plan, committing it, and starting Phase A on tally tracks with their own worktrees). Covers opening tracks and worktrees, installing locked dependencies in them for checks, committing on track branches and landing on local main. Does not cover deployments, APK exports, real customer mail, enabling payments or Phase D's destructive step.
AutoPay and normal online payments are turned off and stay disabled until the maintainer decides to activate them. Agents never enable them or change payment configuration.

Stay on Node 22; production images run node 22 and CI and the packages pin 22. Local checks run in the pinned Node 22.20.0 / npm 11.16.0 container tools/node22-container/run.sh. The Node 24 upgrade is a separate tested step (E3) whose timing the maintainer decides.

G12: old pending online payments created before payments were turned off are marked expired once their pay-by time has passed, only for checkouts never sent to the provider, through the existing expiry path, audited and idempotent, never deleting rows or moving money.

No bank details, payment methods or payment instructions are added or recorded anywhere: not in code, copy, FAQ seeds or emails. The admin records monthly investments under their own category and the client is notified "Investment added".
When the admin records a monthly or earlier investment, the client is also emailed the amount, fund and date, saying it was added to their app and asking them to check it. Corrections send no email.
"Complete all the phases that needs code implementation and leave ones out that needs me." Phase D, E3, releases and the G11 publish were left out.
Question answers are decisions, not tally rules. Tally rules hold only standing constraints that agents must obey, each citing the decision it comes from. Answered questions cite their decision id.

Erasing a client (Q-026). Erasure is refused until the client's invested amount and current value are both zero. Their emails and phones are erased everywhere, including the contact-change history. A client who never completed email verification cannot hold money, so erasing them deletes every record of them. A client who completed email verification is kept as a record with no contact details, and their email and phone can be used again for a new sign-up or a new admin-created client.

Q-030: when a client picks a maturity option in the app, the pick goes to the admin as the client's choice. Nothing changes in money, the ledger or the SIP until the admin confirms, and confirming runs the same resolution as a direct one.
Q-031: the admin fills in the figures for options 2 and 3 before sending the options; the client only picks one. For other figures the client talks to the team and the admin sends new options.
Q-032: when option 3 extends the SIP, the new maturity date is filled in as the old date plus the months added, and the admin can change it before confirming.
Phase G go-ahead: build client erasure (DEC-29) now.

"ok proceed with the next implementations": after Phases F and G, build what remains that needs no maintainer step: the gaps the client and admin experience review still shows on main (U-close, under the DEC-19 delegation) and the carried-forward items such as the APK statement. Phase D, E3, releases and the G11 publish stay with the maintainer.

decisions.text: 2026-11-15, upcoming (not started): nominee by request. A client has at most one nominee (already true in the data model). The client can no longer set, change or remove the nominee directly; instead the client sends a nominee request with name and relation, the admin is notified, and the admin accepts it (the nominee is set) or declines it. The admin can still set or change a nominee directly from the admin panel.

It starts with a read-only audit of each surface; fixes and new work follow from a plan the maintainer approves.

decisions.text: 2026-11-15, next build (recorded, not started): SIP early exit. When a client stops an admin-tracked SIP before its tenure, the admin closes the SIP and returns the money in one action recorded as an early closure, not a maturity, and shown so in the admin and client apps; a maturity date set on that holding is cancelled with it. Today the admin can close a schedule (client page, SIP schedules, Manage, Close the schedule) but can return money only through Mark matured plus Record withdrawal, which records it as a maturity.

decisions.text: An early exit returns the full current value of the client's holding in the SIP's fund. The holding goes to zero; no exit charge and no partial amount.

DEC-43's 'the holding goes to zero' means the value goes to zero.

Small text that sits on the patterned sign-in background or a page gradient (the sign-in footnote, and the 'Values recorded by BeOnEdge ... Investments are subject to market risk.' source and risk line) uses the normal body grey there, so it reaches 4.5:1; the background stays as it is.

decisions.text: The app refuses when an admin tries to suspend or close their own account: the server refuses the request and the admin app hides those actions on the admin's own record. This prevents the sole-admin lockout that today needs a manual database fix (Q-45, carried Q-013). It is a business rule, not a permission or role change (DEC-36), and needs no migration.

decisions.text: Client erasure also replaces the erased client's own known phone numbers in their national forms (for example 98765 43210) inside stored JSON such as idempotency receipts, but only in free-text string values that contain letters or spaces, never in digit-only values such as amounts or ids. Applies to future erasures, plus a one-off re-scrub of already erased accounts if any exist (Q-46, DEC-29).
decisions.status: Built; on main at b2c0970 (lane p-erasure-phones, review-45/48, runtime c0639a1d); ships in 0.18.1. Production from v0.15.4 has no erasures, so no re-scrub is needed there.

decisions.text: Releases follow the maintainer's monthly cycle. Each monthly upgrade session ends in one minor release: November 2026's session is v0.18.0, justified by the size of that month's work. Every later change in the same month ships as a patch of it (0.18.x); no further minor release that month. The next minor, v0.19.0, comes from the December session, scoped by feedback from users and admins, and December's later changes ship as 0.19.x. Production runs v0.15.4 (maintainer, 2026-11-17); the maintainer cuts and deploys every release.
decisions.status: In force from v0.18.0 (cut 2026-11-17): the rest of November ships as 0.18.x; v0.19.0 is the December session.

decisions.text: Both apps get What's new release notes. Client notes cover only what clients see, briefly, in a developer's-note voice; admin notes follow the same style with nothing technical. Notes are bundled in each build, one file per audience, keyed by release version, newest first, with no API, schema or contract change. A sheet shows a release's notes once per user on each device or browser: after an APK update, or at the first signed-in web visit after a deploy (sign-in or session restore). It waits behind other dialogs, the device lock and maintenance, and is remembered when closed; a user with no record sees it. A release with nothing for an audience adds no entry. The notes stay available in Profile > What's new for clients, and on a new admin Account screen opened from the top bar (name, email, role, app version, What's new). Copy has no figures and nothing about payments, AutoPay, bank details or references (DEC-14, DEC-22, DEC-25, DEC-13).
decisions.status: Built; on main at 0b337a0 (lane p-whats-new, reviews 46, 47, 49, runtime 73487af8 and 090981e2); first entry 0.18.1 for both audiences.

decisions.text: The payout outcome form no longer asks for or shows a bank transfer reference, completing UQ-2 as the overhaul plan recommended (field removed) under rule-18: transfers happen outside the app, so the bank holds the reference. The app generates no reference number of its own. The server still accepts and stores a reference that a released admin app sends (rule 11), and references already stored stay in the database; new builds neither ask for nor display them. A payout channel category (in-app payment or outside transfer) is parked until the maintainer resumes payments (DEC-14, DEC-22); when it comes, existing rows are marked outside transfer.
decisions.status: Built; on main at 44a54d4 (lane p-payout-reference, reviews 44 and 50, runtime bf103023 and ca1ed9f1); payout channel category parked; ships in 0.18.1.

decisions.text: The web channels (web and client_web) keep one CSRF token per session: it is issued at sign-in and on refresh rotation, and a CSRF read returns the session's current token instead of replacing it. Reads keep confirming the signed-in user (finding-50). The frontend's one-time CSRF_INVALID recovery from finding-63 stays as a safety net. No API, contract or cookie change; native bearer channels are unchanged.
decisions.status: Built; on main at 623b377 (lane p-csrf-stable, reviews 51 and 56, runtime 9262caf7); cross-tab refresh lock parked to lane p-session-hardening; ships in 0.18.1.

decisions.text: Every build knows its release version. The root VERSION is built into the web bundles and the APK's JavaScript at build time, sent as the x-app-version header and device.appVersion instead of the hard-coded 0.1.0, and shown on the admin Account screen and the client What's new page on every platform. The APK's native versionName stays as set by the release scripts.
decisions.status: Built; on main at 6f495e1 (lane p-app-version, reviews 52 and 53, runtime 08565373 and b9db256d); ships in 0.18.1.

replaced.was: From v0.18.0 every release is a patch release (0.18.x). The main reform is done; what is left is minor changes and fixes, each shipped as a 0.18.x patch. No minor or major version bump unless the maintainer says otherwise.
